questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the "Guess the meaning of the following expressions from the context" list provided before the story begins?
questions.a: The list primes students to notice key lexical items (e.g., "ignominy of retirement", "conical corneas", "pernicious ghost") during reading so they can infer meanings from surrounding sentences rather than relying on a dictionary. A wrong answer (e.g., "to test vocabulary before reading") reveals the student misunderstands that context-based inference is a reading skill, not a pre-test.

questions.q: Explain why knowing that Arundhati Roy is an architect by training and a Booker Prize winner matters for understanding this extract.
questions.a: Roy's architectural training explains the precise, structural descriptions of spaces (the pickle factory, the verandah, the driveway) and her Booker recognition signals that the prose uses dense, layered symbolism (the moth as "pernicious ghost") requiring close reading. A wrong answer (e.g., "it doesn't matter; only the story matters") shows the student overlooks how authorial background shapes narrative style and thematic depth.

questions.q: The textbook mentions Pappachi was an "Imperial Entomologist at the Pusa Institute" whose designation changed to "Joint Director, Entomology" after Independence. Apply this historical detail to predict one conflict Pappachi might face in the story.
questions.a: Pappachi's identity is tied to a British imperial title; losing that title after Independence creates a crisis of status. He may resent his wife's commercial success because it highlights his own diminished authority in the new social order. A wrong answer (e.g., "he will be happy about the promotion") misses the psychological weight of colonial-era designations and the theme of wounded male pride.

questions.q: Compare the phrases "ignominy of retirement" and "pernicious ghost" — what do they reveal about the story's central tension when analyzed together?
questions.a: "Ignominy of retirement" frames Pappachi's public shame as a social event, while "pernicious ghost" internalizes it as a haunting, inescapable presence. Together they suggest the story explores how public humiliation metastasizes into private, generational trauma. A wrong answer treating them as unrelated vocabulary items fails to see the author's pattern of linking external events to psychological haunting.

questions.q: Evaluate the effectiveness of using the "About the Author" blurb (architect, activist, Booker winner) as the sole biographical context for this extract. What is missing?
questions.a: The blurb omits Roy's own Syrian Christian Kerala upbringing, her parents' divorce, and her childhood in Ayemenem — all of which directly inform the story's setting, the Ipe family dynamics, and the critique of patriarchal Syrian Christian households. Relying only on the blurb gives a sanitized, awards-focused view that obscures the autobiographical roots of the narrative. A wrong answer (e.g., "the blurb is sufficient") shows uncritical acceptance of paratext.

questions.q: Create a two-sentence "reading purpose statement" for yourself that incorporates the setting (Ayemenem), the historical moment (post-Independence), and the vocabulary item "taxonomic reshuffle."
questions.a: I will read to discover how a taxonomic reshuffle that erases Pappachi's scientific legacy mirrors the social reshuffle of post-Independence Kerala that erases his patriarchal authority, and how both reshuffles haunt the family's physical spaces in Ayemenem. A weak statement (e.g., "I want to know what happens to the moth") ignores the layered historical and metaphorical dimensions the pre-reading context prepares us for.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Before You Read: Context and ______ is a pre-reading strategy that equips students with the author's biography, historical setting, cultural milieu, and key vocabulary to activate prior knowledge and set a purpose for engaging with the text.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are about to visit a relative's ancestral home in ______ for the first time.
What is Before You Read? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Before You Read: Context and Background is a pre-reading strategy that equips students with the author's biography, historical setting, cultural milieu, and key vocabulary to activate prior knowledge and set a purpose for engaging with the text.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Before You Read?
questions.a: Students often treat "Before You Read" as a skippable formality, guessing vocabulary meanings in isolation without connecting them to the story's themes.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can independently research and summarize the author's background, identify the socio-historical context of the story's setting, explain the meaning of listed lexical items from context clues, and articulate at least two thematic expectations for the reading.
